How we work

A simple, seven-step process

You always know what is happening, what comes next and what we need from you.

Our process
  1. 01

    Discover

    We learn about your business, goals, audience and what success looks like for you.

  2. 02

    Research

    We study your market, competitors and customers to find real opportunities.

  3. 03

    Strategize

    We turn insights into a clear plan with channels, messages, timelines and goals.

  4. 04

    Create

    Our designers, writers and editors bring the plan to life with on-brand creative work.

  5. 05

    Review

    You review the work, share feedback and we refine it until it is right.

  6. 06

    Execute

    We launch campaigns, publish content and go live, keeping you informed at each step.

  7. 07

    Optimize

    We track results, learn what works and improve continuously.

About PIXELBY

A creative studio for brands with big ideas

We are a digital marketing and creative agency that turns ideas into designs, content and campaigns people remember.

Our story

Built on one simple promise: Your Idea, Our Design.

PIXELBY exists for people with ideas: founders launching something new, business owners ready to grow and established brands that want a fresh voice. Our name brings together the pixel, the smallest building block of every digital image, and the idea that great work is built piece by piece, by people who care about the details.

Our mascot, the camera-headed creator in a hoodie, represents how we work: always looking, always creating and always ready to capture the next idea.

Add your founding story here: when PIXELBY started, who started it, why, and a milestone you are proud of. Keep it real and specific.

Mission and vision

Our mission

Help brands grow through meaningful creative work.

We combine strategy, design and content to help businesses communicate clearly, connect with the right audience and grow with confidence.

Our vision

Be the creative partner brands trust to bring ideas to life.

We want every client, from a first-time founder to an established company, to feel that their ideas are understood, respected and turned into work they are proud to share.

Core values

What guides our work

  • Creativity with purpose

    Ideas should look great and also move the business forward.

  • Honesty and transparency

    We set realistic expectations and report results truthfully.

  • Collaboration

    Your knowledge of your business plus our creative skills gives the best results.

  • Attention to detail

    Small details, from spacing to captions, shape how people see a brand.

  • Continuous learning

    Platforms change fast. We keep testing, learning and improving.

  • Results focus

    We measure our work by the outcomes it creates for you.

Creative philosophy

Pixel by pixel, idea by idea.

  1. 01

    Understand first

    Great design starts with listening. We learn your business before we open a design tool.

  2. 02

    Simple beats busy

    Clear messages and clean layouts are easier to remember and easier to act on.

  3. 03

    Bold, but on brand

    We push for ideas that stand out while staying true to who you are.

  4. 04

    Measure and improve

    Creative work is never finished. We test, learn and refine based on real results.

Who we are

This website is operated by PIXELBY ("we", "us", "our"), a digital marketing and creative agency based in Nepal.

Cookies

How long we keep information

We keep enquiry information only for as long as needed to respond to you, provide services or meet legal requirements, after which it is deleted or anonymized.

Your rights

You can ask us to access, correct or delete the personal information we hold about you. Contact us using the details below. We will respond within a reasonable time and in line with applicable law in Nepal, including the Individual Privacy Act, 2075 (2018).

Security

We take reasonable steps to protect your information. However, no method of transmission over the internet is completely secure.

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy from time to time. The latest version will always be available on this page.

Marketing · 1 min read

How to Set Marketing Goals Your Business Can Actually Measure

Vague goals like "get more followers" lead to vague results. Here is a simple way to set goals you can track.

This starter article was written as sample content. Review it, add your own experience and examples, and set a publish date before launch.

Many businesses start marketing with a goal like "grow on social media" or "get more customers". These goals sound good, but they are hard to plan for and impossible to measure. A clear goal tells you what to do, how much to spend and when to change direction.

Use the SMART checklist

A useful goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. Compare these two goals:

  • Weak: "Get more people to know our cafe."
  • Strong: "Get 60 table reservations through Instagram messages in the next 30 days."

The second goal tells you which channel matters, what action counts and when to check progress.

Pick one main metric per goal

Likes and views are easy to see, but they do not always connect to sales. Choose the metric closest to revenue that you can track reliably, such as enquiries, bookings, website form submissions or online orders. Keep reach and engagement as supporting numbers.

Set a baseline first

Before you set a target, look at the last two or three months. How many enquiries did you get per week? Your baseline makes targets realistic and shows whether a campaign actually made a difference.

Review on a schedule

Put a review date in your calendar. Weekly checks are good for ads, monthly checks work for social media. At each review, ask three questions: what worked, what did not, and what will we try next?

Key takeaway: one clear, measurable goal is more useful than five vague ones.

Social Media Tips · 1 min read

7 Social Media Habits That Build Real Engagement

Engagement is not luck. These simple habits help brands build an audience that actually interacts.

This starter article was written as sample content. Review it, add your own experience and examples, and set a publish date before launch.

Algorithms change often, but people do not. Accounts that build real engagement usually follow a few simple habits consistently.

  1. Post on a realistic schedule. Three good posts a week beat daily posts that you cannot keep up.
  2. Hook in the first second. For reels and videos, the opening frame and first line decide whether people keep watching.
  3. Reply to every comment early. Conversations in the first hour signal that your post is worth showing to more people.
  4. Mix your content. Combine helpful tips, behind-the-scenes moments, customer stories and offers. Not every post should sell.
  5. Write captions for humans. Ask a simple question or give a clear next step, such as "Save this for later" or "Send us a message".
  6. Use your analytics. Check which posts get saves and shares. Those are strong signs that content is valuable.
  7. Stay on brand. Consistent colors, fonts and tone help people recognize your posts before they read your name.

Start small

Choose two habits from this list and practice them for a month. Then add another. Consistency over time matters more than any single viral post.

Branding · 1 min read

Logo vs Brand Identity: What Is the Difference?

A logo is only one part of your brand. Learn what a full brand identity includes and why it matters.

This starter article was written as sample content. Review it, add your own experience and examples, and set a publish date before launch.

People often use "logo" and "brand" as if they mean the same thing. They are connected, but they are not the same.

The logo

A logo is a symbol, wordmark or combination of both that identifies your business. It is like your signature: important, but small.

The brand identity

A brand identity is the full visual and verbal system that makes your business recognizable everywhere. It usually includes:

  • Logo and its variations for different sizes and backgrounds
  • Color palette with exact color codes
  • Typography for headings and body text
  • Graphic elements such as patterns, icons or illustration style
  • Photography and video style
  • Tone of voice, meaning how your brand writes and speaks

Why brand guidelines matter

Brand guidelines document all of these rules in one place. When your team, printer or a new designer follows the same guide, every post, banner and package looks like it came from the same brand. That consistency builds recognition and trust over time.

Key takeaway: start with a strong logo, but invest in a full identity system if you want your brand to look professional everywhere.

Content Creation · 1 min read

Plan a Month of Content in One Afternoon

A simple four-step method to plan a full month of posts without daily stress.

This starter article was written as sample content. Review it, add your own experience and examples, and set a publish date before launch.

Deciding what to post every morning is stressful and leads to rushed content. Batch planning solves that. Here is a method you can finish in one afternoon.

1. Choose three to five content pillars

Pillars are the main topics your brand talks about. A restaurant might choose: signature dishes, behind the kitchen, customer moments and offers.

2. List important dates

Add festivals, holidays, product launches and events for the month. In Nepal, festivals like Dashain, Tihar and Holi can shape what your audience wants to see.

3. Fill a simple calendar

Use a spreadsheet with columns for date, pillar, format (post, carousel, reel, story), idea, caption and status. Spread your pillars evenly across the weeks.

4. Batch the production

Shoot all photos in one session, record several videos together and write captions in one sitting. Batching saves hours compared with creating one post at a time.

Leave room for real time

Keep one or two open slots each week for trends and timely moments. A plan should guide you, not trap you.

Business Growth · 1 min read

When Is the Right Time to Hire a Marketing Agency?

Signs that your business is ready for outside marketing help, and how to prepare.

This starter article was written as sample content. Review it, add your own experience and examples, and set a publish date before launch.

Many business owners handle marketing themselves at the start. That is normal. But as the business grows, doing everything alone can slow you down.

Signs you may be ready

  • You post inconsistently because daily operations take all your time.
  • Your visuals look different on every platform.
  • You are spending on ads but do not know whether they work.
  • You are launching a new product, service or location.
  • Your social media is not bringing enquiries.

How to prepare

Before you contact an agency, write down your goals, your budget range, your target customers and examples of brands you like. This helps the agency give you an accurate proposal.

Questions to ask an agency

  • Can you show work similar to what we need?
  • Who will work on our account?
  • How will you report results, and how often?
  • What exactly is included in the price?

Key takeaway: the right time to hire help is when marketing is important to growth but you cannot give it the time or skills it needs.
